title: Feasibility and tolerability of the HomeSleepTest audio for suppressing REM sleep in in-patient patients with unipolar depression in everyday clinical practice
summary:
Depression is often accompanied by changes in sleep patterns, particularly in what is known as REM sleep (dream sleep, ‘Rapid Eye Movement’). Many antidepressants also affect this phase of sleep. A well-known, rapidly effective method for the short-term treatment of severe depression is what is known as sleep deprivation, in which a patient is kept awake for one night. However, this method is stressful for patients and requires significant staffing resources, as constant monitoring is necessary. A gentler alternative could be the targeted suppression of REM sleep, whilst preserving the other, restorative sleep phases. Initial studies show that such selective REM sleep suppression can reduce depressive symptoms.
The present study is being conducted in collaboration with SOMNOmedics AG, which has developed a system (HST audio, SOMNOmedics AG) that automatically detects REM sleep and interrupts it using acoustic signals. In a previous study conducted by SOMNOmedics involving healthy adults, the procedure proved to be feasible, safe and well tolerated. The aim of this study is to investigate the clinical applicability, safety and patient compliance of a treatment protocol for automated REM sleep disruption using HST audio in in-patient patients with unipolar depression.
conditions: Severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms
Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode mild
Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate
Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms

interventions.name: Selective suppression of REM sleep (2 nights a week for 4 weeks) using acoustic signals and automated REM sleep detection (HomeSleepTest audio, SOMNOmedics AG, Randersacker, Germany)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosis of unipolar depression (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, F32.8, F33.0, F33.1, F33.2, F34.1)
2. Medically justifiable ability (in the opinion of the treatment team) to refrain from making any changes to medication with tricyclic antidepressants, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors during the study period
3. Capacity to give consent
4. Written informed consent from study participants following verbal and written information.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Irregular or altered use of psychotropic drugs, in particular antidepressants and other medicines that may affect sleep, within the last two weeks.
2. Acute intoxication or withdrawal from alcohol (F10), opioids (F11), cannabinoids (F12), sedatives or hypnotics (F13), cocaine (F14), stimulants (F15), hallucinogens (F16), volatile solvents (F18) or a combination thereof (F19), excluding tobacco and caffeine.
3. Psychiatric disorders:
a. Schizophrenia (F20) or schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (F21, F22, F23, F25)
b. Bipolar disorder (F31), mania (F30) or cyclothymia (F34.0)
c. Acute suicidal ideation (R45.81) or intentional self-harm (X60–X84).
4. Sleep disorders:
a. Untreated severe sleep apnoea: either reported by the patient or where an oxygen desaturation index (ODI) ≥ 15 is measured during the first night’s OtwoFellow monitoring.
b. Organic insomnia/hyposomnia (G47.0), hypersomnia (G47.1), circadian sleep-wake rhythm disorders (G47.2), narcolepsy or cataplexy (G47.3)
5. Epilepsy (G40)
6. Severe cardiovascular, neurological, gastrointestinal or malignant conditions requiring medical treatment, excluding successfully managed chronic conditions, in particular high blood pressure and diabetes.
7. Shift work within the last three months or travel across a meridian lasting more than one week within the month prior to the start of the study.
8. Pregnancy (as determined by beta-hCG).
